$comment: EXP-1341/NEW-2: ONE session model. Every session is a `sessions` row run by the same engine. NEW-2: a team agent is a DEFINITION (`agents`), never a session; it runs as conversation sessions, roots with `agentId` set (one per agent and member). sessionKindOf(session) = `agent` when `agentId` is set, else `thread`; sessionTraits(kind) reads `kinds`; an unknown kind = `thread`. A conversation session is `persistent` (never ends: an exit or a refused launch reports `idle`, `sessions.end` refuses it, its scratch dir is kept, a message resumes the SAME row, and its device REVIVES it when it comes back). FEED-134: a thread's ROOT survives its process too (the conversation IS the thread): its device's `ended` report (an app quit, a daemon stop, a crash) reads `idle`, a message to an ended root revives the SAME row, and only a person's End or the agent's own `sessions.end` ends it; a thread's CHILD still ends with its process (a worker whose report reaches its parent) and a message to an ended child continues as its sibling. `triggers` live on the agent definition and are fired by the SERVER (`lib/agents/triggers.ts`), never by the device. Mirrors: TS src/session-kind.ts, desktop `domain::session_kind`, iOS ExpCore `SessionKind.swift`, Android `domain/SessionKind.kt`; the server and the device branch on these traits, never on the kind string. EXP-1686 (owner 2026-11-04): `linksIssues` = a `session_issues` row may land on the session. A conversation session never holds one (they would accumulate forever): issues sent to it arrive as a MESSAGE (session-brief.json ISSUE BRIEF) and nothing else; its children and the threads it starts are `thread` and link as ever. A link naming a conversation is refused over MCP; over tRPC it delivers the same message (older clients still draw a "+").
